## The claim

P4-27: a BUB1B loss-of-function expression signature is reversed by at least one approved drug in two independent connectivity engines, and specifically to that signature

**Prediction if true.** Signature fixed before any drug query: the LINCS L1000 BUB1B loss-of-function consensus signature (CRISPR knockout if SigCom LINCS holds one, else shRNA), its 100 most raised and 100 most lowered genes; if LINCS holds none, the GEO human BUB1B knockdown series named in step-9 research/data-sources.md. At least one approved drug (ChEMBL max phase 4 or an openFDA label), aggregated per compound by its best signature rank, is in the top 100 reversers of both SigCom LINCS (l1000_cp) and iLINCS, and is in the top 100 reversers of at most 1 of 20 size-matched random-gene decoy signatures run through SigCom. Positive control, required for the result to count: queried against the genetic-perturbation library, the signature ranks at least one other checkpoint-gene loss (BUB1, BUB3, MAD2L1, MAD1L1, TTK) in the top 5 % of mimickers

**What would refute it.** No approved drug is in both engines' top 100 reversers, or every such drug is also in the top 100 reversers of 2 or more of the 20 decoys. If the positive control fails, the run is recorded as uninterpretable, never as support

## Evidence

Nothing observed yet. This claim is proposed, not tested.
